title: Always On Availability Groups
description: Configure and manage Always On Availability Groups for high availability and disaster recovery in SQL Server.

data.text: Always On Availability Groups (AGs) are the flagship high-availability feature in SQL Server. An AG groups one or more user databases into a failover unit. Each database in the group replicates between one primary replica and up to eight secondary replicas. If the primary replica fails, the group can fail over to a secondary replica, keeping your applications running with minimal downtime.

data.title: Enterprise vs. Standard Edition
data.text: Always On AGs are available in both Enterprise and Standard editions, though Standard Edition limits you to a Basic AG with one database and no automatic failover. Enterprise Edition unlocks up to eight secondary replicas and multiple Availability Group Listeners.

items: Availability Group (AG): A container for one or more databases that fail over together.
Availability Replica: A hosted instance of the AG. One replica is primary; others are secondary.
Availability Group Listener: A virtual network name that enables client applications to connect without knowing the current primary replica.
Quorum: A voting mechanism that ensures the AG cluster has enough nodes to make a failover decision and prevents split-brain scenarios.

data.caption: Always On Availability Group topology with one primary, two secondary replicas, and a listener
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[Client App] --> B[AG Listener]
    B --> C[Primary Replica]
    B --> D[Secondary Replica 1]
    B --> E[Secondary Replica 2]
    C --> F[User DB]
    D --> G[User DB Readable Secondary]
    E --> H[User DB Readable Secondary]
    I[Cluster Nodes] --> C
    I --> D
    I --> E

data.text: Each secondary replica can operate in either synchronous-commit or asynchronous-commit mode. Synchronous mode guarantees that transactions are committed on both primary and secondary before acknowledging to the client, which protects data but adds latency. Asynchronous mode acknowledges the client after the primary commits and sends changes to the secondary without waiting, which minimizes latency but can lose recent transactions during failover.

cards.title: Synchronous Commit
cards.description: Waits for each secondary replica to harden the log before acknowledging the client.
cons: Can be slowed by slow network links

cards.title: Asynchronous Commit
cards.description: Acknowledges the client immediately after the primary commits without waiting for secondaries.

data.title: Quorum Is Critical
data.text: Always On uses a quorum-based voting system. If the cluster loses quorum, the AG goes offline, not into a split-brain state. Ensure you have enough cluster nodes and configure an appropriate quorum model (node majority, node and file share majority, etc.) before going live.

data.title: Create an Availability Group with T-SQL
data.content: This example creates an AG named AG_Sales with one primary and two secondary replicas using synchronous commit.
data.code:
CREATE AVAILABILITY GROUP AG_Sales
FOR
(
    DATABASE SalesDB
)
REPLICA ON
    N'SQL01' WITH
    (
        ENDPOINT_URL = N'tcp://SQL01:5022',
        AVAILABILITY_MODE = SYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT,
        FAILOVER_MODE = AUTOMATIC,
        SEEDING_MODE = AUTOMATIC
    ),
    N'SQL02' WITH
    (
        ENDPOINT_URL = N'tcp://SQL02:5022',
        AVAILABILITY_MODE = SYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT,
        FAILOVER_MODE = AUTOMATIC,
        SEEDING_MODE = AUTOMATIC
    ),
    N'SQL03' WITH
    (
        ENDPOINT_URL = N'tcp://SQL03:5022',
        AVAILABILITY_MODE = ASYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT,
        FAILOVER_MODE = MANUAL,
        SEEDING_MODE = AUTOMATIC
    );

data.title: Key DMVs and Tools
items: sys.availability_groups: Returns one row per AG in the failover instance.
sys.dm_hadr_database_replica_states: Provides per-replica health, synchronization state, and log send/redo queue information.
sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states: Tells you the role and connection state of each replica.
Always On Dashboard (SSMS): Visual summary of AG health, synchronization state, and failover readiness.

data.title: Always On AG Key Points
points: Always On AGs protect user databases with automatic or manual failover.
Use synchronous commit when data loss is unacceptable; use asynchronous for geo-distributed replicas.
The listener provides a stable connection point for client applications.
Quorum voting prevents split-brain scenarios during network partitions.
Monitor AG health with DMVs and the Always On Dashboard.
data.takeaway: Design your AG topology around RPO and RTO goals. Synchronous replicas near the primary give you zero data loss with automatic failover, while asynchronous replicas extend geographic reach at the cost of potential data loss.
